text: John Lennon's psychedelic Rolls-Royce, a bespoke Phantom V limousine ordered in December 1964 from R.S. Mead Ltd in Maidenhead, was delivered in June 1965 and originally painted matte black with a chrome grille. After being damaged during Lennon's six-week filming stint in Spain in late 1966, the car was repainted bright yellow in April 1967 by artist Steve Weaver, who applied elaborate Romany-inspired floral and zodiac motifs, including Libra on the roof, at a cost of £290 (equivalent to £6,649 in 2023). The design, described as a "lurid Romany floral/zodiac hybrid" and "Romany Gypsy style, with elements of the psychedelic era," became a sensation and was first displayed on 28 May 1967 at a party for Brian Epstein. Lennon and Yoko Ono donated the car to the Cooper-Hewitt Museum in December 1977 for a $250,000 tax deduction, though disputes over the credit value with the IRS continued into 1987. In June 1985, the car was auctioned by Sotheby's in New York for US$2,299,000—then the highest price ever paid for a car—and purchased by Canadian businessman Jim Pattison, who used it to promote Expo 86 in Vancouver. Pattison later donated it to the Province of British Columbia, where it was exhibited at the Transportation Museum of British Columbia until 1993 and then transferred to the Royal British Columbia Museum, where it has remained since. The vehicle has been widely exhibited at institutions including the Cooper-Hewitt Museum, the National Museum of American History, the Pointe-à-Callière Museum in Montréal, the Pacific National Exhibition in Vancouver, and Bonhams in London. The yellow paint, made from common latex house paint, is fragile and requires careful handling; museum staff avoid polishing and use tiny brushes for touch-ups, and the car must be run at least once a year to maintain its moving parts, as movement risks damaging the paint. After years of inactivity and poor maintenance, including clogged carburetors, the car underwent repairs in 2020 and now runs smoothly, described by a mechanic as "purring like a kitten in a creamery." The Beatles were formed in Liverpool in 1960, with Ringo Starr joining by 1962, and Beatlemania began in the UK in 1963, spreading globally in 1964, making all members wealthy. Lennon had previously owned a used black and maroon Rolls-Royce in July 1964 and decided to buy the new Phantom V by December 1964. The finished car is 19 feet 10 inches long, 6 feet 7 inches wide, and weighs almost three metric tons. It features a 6.23-litre V8 engine, black leather upholstery, a cocktail cabinet, writing table, reading lamps, a seven-piece luggage set, a Perdio TV, a refrigerator in the trunk, and tinted windows. In December 1965, Lennon added a convertible back seat, large ashtrays, a Philips floating record player, an 8-track tape player, an upgraded Sony TV, and a radio telephone, including a public address system for shouting to passersby. The car was used by the Beatles to travel to Buckingham Palace on 26 October 1965 for their MBE honours. Lennon did not have a driving licence when he ordered the car but obtained one within a few months and hired Les Anthony as his driver and bodyguard. Lennon's psychedelic Rolls-Royce is now owned by the Royal British Columbia Museum in Victoria, British Columbia.
